re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +817
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T21:34:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

content.text:
# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox): reproduce the incident shape — guest PR, validation cancelled by a simulated kicker race, no pushes — assert the machine re-dispatches and the required check reports without any human push. *Hook: E2E scenario `cancelled-validation-guest-pr`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded 19:08Z agents timeline (log lines quoted in this issue) — all four machine PRs defer on the phantom; after the fix, the replay arms the FIFO head within one tick. *Hook: REG fixture from the live log; CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even with green UT/IT/E2E.*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..2` — reconciliation function; conclusion mapping (success/failure/cancelled/timeout). Maps AC1, AC3.
- `IT-1..3` — two-tick phantom self-heal (AC2); cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe (AC3); clone-failure backoff → degraded flag (I5).
- `E2E-1` — sandbox guest-PR cancellation loop (AC4).
- `E2E-2` — sandbox machine-PR queue: phantom injected mid-queue, detection + heal + continue.
- `REG-1` — recorded live-timeline replay (AC5). **CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are green** — the bug's signature is queue shape, only REG sees it.
- Shared assertions run through old and new mutex paths for one release cycle (semantic-drift property: identical arming decisions).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Holder PR labeled armed but its validation run is `in_progress` and healthy: NOT a phantom; deferral is legitimate — the sweeper must not steal the slot.
- **E2** — Two ticks race on the registry (parallel SM runs): last-reconciled-wins is safe because both derive from the same label+run truth.
- **E3** — gh-748 dedupe vs cancellation storm (kicker flapping): re-dispatch at most once per tick per PR, with a flap counter and escalating backoff — cure must not amplify the race.
- **E4** — GitHub API failure mid-reconciliation: retry; worst case one extra deferral tick (degradation), never a wedge.
- **E5** — PR force-pushed while armed: head change un-arms per existing park semantics (family: #994's reset rule) and releases the slot — cross-card interaction tested explicitly.

## Non-goals

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +817
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T21:34:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

blocks.text:
# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox): reproduce the incident shape — guest PR, validation cancelled by a simulated kicker race, no pushes — assert the machine re-dispatches and the required check reports without any human push. *Hook: E2E scenario `cancelled-validation-guest-pr`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded 19:08Z agents timeline (log lines quoted in this issue) — all four machine PRs defer on the phantom; after the fix, the replay arms the FIFO head within one tick. *Hook: REG fixture from the live log; CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even with green UT/IT/E2E.*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..2` — reconciliation function; conclusion mapping (success/failure/cancelled/timeout). Maps AC1, AC3.
- `IT-1..3` — two-tick phantom self-heal (AC2); cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe (AC3); clone-failure backoff → degraded flag (I5).
- `E2E-1` — sandbox guest-PR cancellation loop (AC4).
- `E2E-2` — sandbox machine-PR queue: phantom injected mid-queue, detection + heal + continue.
- `REG-1` — recorded live-timeline replay (AC5). **CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are green** — the bug's signature is queue shape, only REG sees it.
- Shared assertions run through old and new mutex paths for one release cycle (semantic-drift property: identical arming decisions).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Holder PR labeled armed but its validation run is `in_progress` and healthy: NOT a phantom; deferral is …

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +817
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T21:34:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox): reproduce the incident shape — guest PR, validation cancelled by a simulated kicker race, no pushes — assert the machine re-dispatches and the required check reports without any human push. *Hook: E2E scenario `cancelled-validation-guest-pr`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded 19:08Z agents timeline (log lines quoted in this issue) — all four machine PRs defer on the phantom; after the fix, the replay arms the FIFO head within one tick. *Hook: REG fixture from the live log; CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even with green UT/IT/E2E.*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..2` — reconciliation function; conclusion mapping (success/failure/cancelled/timeout). Maps AC1, AC3.
- `IT-1..3` — two-tick phantom self-heal (AC2); cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe (AC3); clone-failure backoff → degraded flag (I5).
- `E2E-1` — sandbox guest-PR cancellation loop (AC4).
- `E2E-2` — sandbox machine-PR queue: phantom injected mid-queue, detection + heal + continue.
- `REG-1` — recorded live-timeline replay (AC5). **CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are green** — the bug's signature is queue shape, only REG sees it.
- Shared assertions run through old and new mutex paths for one release cycle (semantic-drift property: identical arming decisions).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Holder PR labeled armed but its validation run is `in_progress` and healthy: NOT a phantom; deferral is …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +817
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T21:34:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox): reproduce the incident shape — guest PR, validation cancelled by a simulated kicker race, no pushes — assert the machine re-dispatches and the required check reports without any human push. *Hook: E2E scenario `cancelled-validation-guest-pr`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded 19:08Z agents timeline (log lines quoted in this issue) — all four machine PRs defer on the phantom; after the fix, the replay arms the FIFO head within one tick. *Hook: REG fixture from the live log; CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even with green UT/IT/E2E.*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..2` — reconciliation function; conclusion mapping (success/failure/cancelled/timeout). Maps AC1, AC3.
- `IT-1..3` — two-tick phantom self-heal (AC2); cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe (AC3); clone-failure backoff → degraded flag (I5).
- `E2E-1` — sandbox guest-PR cancellation loop (AC4).
- `E2E-2` — sandbox machine-PR queue: phantom injected mid-queue, detection + heal + continue.
- `REG-1` — recorded live-timeline replay (AC5). **CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are green** — the bug's signature is queue shape, only REG sees it.
- Shared assertions run through old and new mutex paths for one release cycle (semantic-drift property: identical arming decisions).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Holder PR labeled armed but its validation run is `in_progress` and healthy: NOT a phantom; deferral is …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +817
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T21:34:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox): reproduce the incident shape — guest PR, validation cancelled by a simulated kicker race, no pushes — assert the machine re-dispatches and the required check reports without any human push. *Hook: E2E scenario `cancelled-validation-guest-pr`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded 19:08Z agents timeline (log lines quoted in this issue) — all four machine PRs defer on the phantom; after the fix, the replay arms the FIFO head within one tick. *Hook: REG fixture from the live log; CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even with green UT/IT/E2E.*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..2` — reconciliation function; conclusion mapping (success/failure/cancelled/timeout). Maps AC1, AC3.
- `IT-1..3` — two-tick phantom self-heal (AC2); cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe (AC3); clone-failure backoff → degraded flag (I5).
- `E2E-1` — sandbox guest-PR cancellation loop (AC4).
- `E2E-2` — sandbox machine-PR queue: phantom injected mid-queue, detection + heal + continue.
- `REG-1` — recorded live-timeline replay (AC5). **CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are green** — the bug's signature is queue shape, only REG sees it.
- Shared assertions run through old and new mutex paths for one release cycle (semantic-drift property: identical arming decisions).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Holder PR labeled armed but its validation run is `in_progress` and healthy: NOT a phantom; deferral is …

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments.
