crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

blocks.text:
`cli_execute_command` is a host tool (dmtools) — likely executed via shell. The `--ref ' + (ticket.branch || '')` interpolation: existing code at line 1878 does the same pattern with branchName, so it's an established codebase pattern. But branch is guest-controlled on guest PRs. `gh workflow run ... --ref $(curl evil)`? Branch names in git cannot contain spaces? Actually they CAN contain some shell metachars (`;`, `&`, `$()`, backticks are allowed in ref names? check-ref-format disallows: control chars, space? Let me recall precisely — git check-ref-format component rules: cannot begin/end with '/', cannot contain '..', control chars (0x00-0x1F), ', '~', '^', ':', '?', '*', '[', '\\'. Wait is space disallowed? Yes! "They cannot contain space" — refname rules: no space allowed? Hmm. Actually I recall space IS disallowed in ref names. Let me think: check-ref-format disallows ASCII control chars, space, ~ ^ : ? * [ \ and .. sequences. Yes, space is disallowed. But `;`, `&`, `|`, `$`, backtick are allowed! e.g. branch name `x;id;y` — is `;` allowed in a ref? The disallowed list doesn't include `;`. So a guest could create a branch named `$(id)` — wait `$()` contains `(` and `)` which are allowed. So a malicious guest branch `a$(touch /tmp/pwn)` could inject via the SM shell when it dispatches validation. BUT: (a) the SM only processes machine-tracked PRs? The rerun_canceled_checks applies to PRs in the factory flow, including guest PRs (gh-757 context says guest PRs are in the machine flow but no pushes). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +817
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T21:34:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

blocks.text:
# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox): reproduce the incident shape — guest PR, validation cancelled by a simulated kicker race, no pushes — assert the machine re-dispatches and the required check reports without any human push. *Hook: E2E scenario `cancelled-validation-guest-pr`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded 19:08Z agents timeline (log lines quoted in this issue) — all four machine PRs defer on the phantom; after the fix, the replay arms the FIFO head within one tick. *Hook: REG fixture from the live log; CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even with green UT/IT/E2E.*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..2` — reconciliation function; conclusion mapping (success/failure/cancelled/timeout). Maps AC1, AC3.
- `IT-1..3` — two-tick phantom self-heal (AC2); cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe (AC3); clone-failure backoff → degraded flag (I5).
- `E2E-1` — sandbox guest-PR cancellation loop (AC4).

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +817
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T21:34:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox): reproduce the incident shape — guest PR, validation cancelled by a simulated kicker race, no pushes — assert the machine re-dispatches and the required check reports without any human push. *Hook: E2E scenario `cancelled-validation-guest-pr`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded 19:08Z agents timeline (log lines quoted in this issue) — all four machine PRs defer on the phantom; after the fix, the replay arms the FIFO head within one tick. *Hook: REG fixture from the live log; CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even with green UT/IT/E2E.*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..2` — reconciliation function; conclusion mapping (success/failure/cancelled/timeout). Maps AC1, AC3.
- `IT-1..3` — two-tick phantom self-heal (AC2); cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe (AC3); clone-failure backoff → degraded flag (I5).
- `E2E-1` — sandbox guest-PR cancellation loop (AC4).
- `E2E-2` — sandbox machine-PR queue: phantom injected mid-queue, detection + heal + continue.
- `REG-1` — recorded live-timeline replay (AC5). **CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are green** — the bug's signature is queue shape, only REG sees it.
- Shared assertions run through old and new mutex paths for one release cycle (semantic-drift property: identical arming decisions).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Holder PR labeled armed but its validation run is `in_progress` and healthy: NOT a phantom; deferral is …

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

blocks.text:
`cli_execute_command` is a host tool (dmtools) — likely executed via shell. The `--ref ' + (ticket.branch || '')` interpolation: existing code at line 1878 does the same pattern with branchName, so it's an established codebase pattern. But branch is guest-controlled on guest PRs. `gh workflow run ... --ref $(curl evil)`? Branch names in git cannot contain spaces? Actually they CAN contain some shell metachars (`;`, `&`, `$()`, backticks are allowed in ref names? check-ref-format disallows: control chars, space? Let me recall precisely — git check-ref-format component rules: cannot begin/end with '/', cannot contain '..', control chars (0x00-0x1F), ', '~', '^', ':', '?', '*', '[', '\\'. Wait is space disallowed? Yes! "They cannot contain space" — refname rules: no space allowed? Hmm. Actually I recall space IS disallowed in ref names. Let me think: check-ref-format disallows ASCII control chars, space, ~ ^ : ? * [ \ and .. sequences. Yes, space is disallowed. But `;`, `&`, `|`, `$`, backtick are allowed! e.g. branch name `x;id;y` — is `;` allowed in a ref? The disallowed list doesn't include `;`. So a guest could create a branch named `$(id)` — wait `$()` contains `(` and `)` which are allowed. So a malicious guest branch `a$(touch /tmp/pwn)` could inject via the SM shell when it dispatches validation. BUT: (a) the SM only processes machine-tracked PRs? The rerun_canceled_checks applies to PRs in the factory flow, including guest PRs (gh-757 context says guest PRs are in the machine flow but no pushes). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +817
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T21:34:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

blocks.text:
# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*

pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +817
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T21:34:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# gh-1000: Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

## Goal — the validation mutex holder is always resolvable to a live PR, and a CANCELLED validation is a validation that never happened (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **every holder of the `ai_validating` mutex resolves to an open PR that provably carries the armed state, and every validation run that ends CANCELLED is re-dispatched as if it never ran** — a queue where all candidates defer forever, and a PR whose only sin is a cancelled run, become unreachable states.

Today two divergences wedge the agents queue simultaneously. (1) The mutex registry reports `slots 1/1 taken` on every SM tick while NO open PR carries the `ai_validating` label and the published factory state says `lanes.validating: []` — the holder is unresolvable, so every candidate logs `🔒 mutex "ai_validating" slots 1/1 taken — candidate pr-N defers` and no validation ever arms: no machine PR gets validated, no rework legs start, the queue drains at zero. (2) A validation run concluded CANCELLED (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 class) is treated as concluded-with-verdict: the SM reasons "no context reads CANCELLED on <sha> — nothing to rerun", the required `crap` check never reports, the ruleset refuses merge (`Required status check "crap" is expected`), and — because the PR is guest-authored — no machine push will ever create a new head to escape. Both were live 2026-10-17 ~19:08Z and blocked all four open machine PRs plus the owner's #997 at once.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the mutex is just an optimization; trust the logs." The mutex IS the gate — when its registry diverges from label/lane truth it becomes a phantom turnstile that costs a full queue, so its correctness is the subject of this card, not a side note.
- **Retracted:** "CANCELLED means 'someone else owns this; hands off'." A cancelled run produced NO verdict about the tree; treating it as concluded is how #997 got parked with green intent. Cancellation is an absence of validation, and the machine must behave accordingly.
- **Retracted (family note):** any human workaround — hand-clearing labels, hand-pushing empty commits to unstick PRs, hand-closing leaked checks. All three earlier instances (#994, #998, this one) were papered over by the operator before the owner banned it; this card assumes from the start that the only acceptable cure is in the machine.

## Architecture

Named state objects and the single-writer rule (the SUBJECT of every verb is the **mutex registry entry** / the **validation-run record**, never the PR at large):

```
sources of truth (per PR):
  L = label layer      (ai_validating on the PR)
  P = published lanes  (factory state: lanes.validating)
  M = mutex registry   (in-memory slots, per SM process)

INVARIANT (single-writer): M is DERIVED, never primary.
  derive(M) = { pr | L[pr]=armed ∧ validation_run(pr) not concluded }
  on every tick, M := derive(M)   [reconciliation, not caching]

tick flow:
  reconcile M from L + run states
  for each candidate in FIFO:
      if holder(M) resolves ∧ holder ≠ candidate → defer (legitimate)
      if holder(M) unresolvable → self-heal + ALARM (never silent full-defer)
  validation run conclusion mapping:
      success/failure → verdict (latch, unarm)
      CANCELLED       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch (same head, gh-748 guard)
      timed_out       → NO verdict → unarm + re-dispatch + count metric
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests):**
- **I1 — resolvable holder:** at every tick boundary, every mutex holder resolves to an open PR whose label state matches the held slot. `slots 1/1 taken` with zero labeled PRs is unreachable.
- **I2 — self-heal with alarm:** if reconciliation finds M ⊄ derive(M), the registry is corrected in the same tick and an alarm record (machine log + factory state `mutex_self_heals` counter) is emitted. Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks while M is non-empty and unresolvable is itself an alarm condition.
- **I3 — cancellation carries no verdict:** a CANCELLED run contributes nothing to `latestVerdict`; the validation record returns to `not-dispatched`; the arm stays or re-dispatches per gh-748 dedupe (same-head, same-run-context suppression, not blanket "nothing to rerun").
- **I4 — guest PRs benefit too:** cancellation-retry is authorship-blind; the gh-757 guest restriction applies to machine *pushes*, never to machine *re-dispatch of validation the machine itself cancelled*.
- **I5 — update_branch hygiene:** silent-update clone failures retry with backoff and a cleaned workspace; after N failures the PR is flagged `silent-update-degraded` (visible state) instead of being silently retried forever.

## Capability surface (every divergence → handling obligation)

| Divergence / outcome | Handling today | Must do (this card) | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutex holder not in label layer | silent full-defer, wedge | reconcile + self-heal + alarm (I2) | core |
| Mutex holder's PR closed/merged | unknown (same path) | release slot + alarm | core |
| Validation CANCELLED | "nothing to rerun", park forever | unarm + re-dispatch (I3) | core |
| Validation timed_out | unknown | same as CANCELLED | core |
| Silent-update clone failure (/tmp) | raw exit 1, no retry semantics | backoff retry + degraded flag (I5) | core |
| All candidates defer ≥2 ticks | normal log line | alarm record | core |
| Mutex metric exposure | none | `mutex_self_heals`, `phantom_holder_ticks` in factory state | second tier |

**Excluded (rationale):** parallel validation slots (a policy decision beyond this card — the serial slot is intentional); auto-push for guest PRs (gh-757 stands — but note the card then REQUIRES I4 so guest PRs are never stranded by machine-caused cancellations).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: `derive(M)` from fixture label/run states — including the live 19:08Z shape (registry says 1/1, labels say none) — returns ∅ and flags the phantom. *Hook: pure reconciliation UT with recorded fixture.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake API): two consecutive ticks with an unresolvable holder → registry self-heals, `phantom_holder_ticks` increments, an alarm record lands, and a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick. *Hook: scripted two-tick scenario.*
- **AC3** — Cancellation: a run transitioning to CANCELLED on head H leaves the validation record `not-dispatched`; the next tick re-dispatches (gh-748 dedupe permits suppression only for an already-queued dispatch of the same head); the PR never enters the "no context reads CANCELLED — nothing to rerun" branch. *Hook: scripted run-lifecycle fixture.*
- **AC4** — End-to-end (sandbox): reproduce the incident shape — guest PR, validation cancelled by a simulated kicker race, no pushes — assert the machine re-dispatches and the required check reports without any human push. *Hook: E2E scenario `cancelled-validation-guest-pr`.*
- **AC5** — Regression: replay the recorded 19:08Z agents timeline (log lines quoted in this issue) — all four machine PRs defer on the phantom; after the fix, the replay arms the FIFO head within one tick. *Hook: REG fixture from the live log; CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even with green UT/IT/E2E.*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..2` — reconciliation function; conclusion mapping (success/failure/cancelled/timeout). Maps AC1, AC3.
- `IT-1..3` — two-tick phantom self-heal (AC2); cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe (AC3); clone-failure backoff → degraded flag (I5).
- `E2E-1` — sandbox guest-PR cancellation loop (AC4).
- `E2E-2` — sandbox machine-PR queue: phantom injected mid-queue, detection + heal + continue.
- `REG-1` — recorded live-timeline replay (AC5). **CI rule: red REG blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are green** — the bug's signature is queue shape, only REG sees it.
- Shared assertions run through old and new mutex paths for one release cycle (semantic-drift property: identical arming decisions).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Holder PR labeled armed but its validation run is `in_progress` and healthy: NOT a phantom; deferral is …

Now let me look at the important issues:

1. **The alarm object**: In githubSource.js, `divergent.alarm` is the alarm from `reconcile()`. `reconcile()` returns `alarm: { type, label, repo, holders: {cached, live}, at }` — there is NO `title` or `detail` field! But githubSource logs `alarm.title` and `alarm.detail`:
```js
console.log('  ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ...)
```
This prints "⚠️ null — null — ..." (actually "⚠️ undefined — undefined"). Bug: reconcile()'s alarm object has type/label/repo/holders/at, no title/detail. So the log line would be `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ...)`. That's a correctness issue — the alarm title/detail are undefined. Actually String concatenation of undefined gives "undefined". That's BLOCKING-ish? It's a logging bug — the alarm record lands malformed in log. It's a real bug: the code references fields that don't exist on the alarm shape defined in mutexRegistry.reconcile. Severity: IMPORTANT at least — log line garbage, but does it break anything? `alarm.title` is undefined; concat produces "⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders...)". Misleading alarm log. I'd call it IMPORTANT (works, but alarm line is garbage). Actually wait — is there any place where alarm has title/detail? `recordPhantomHeal` builds alarm with type/label/holders/at. mergeSnapshot merges alarms. No title/detail anywhere. So yes, the log line prints "undefined — undefined". Also the recordMutexTickEvent stores `alarm` (the reconcile alarm with type etc.).

Also `console.log('  ⚠️ ' + alarm.title ...)` — note in derive/reconcile, alarm fields: type: 'phantom_mutex_holder'. The log should probably use alarm.type. This is a genuine bug worth flaging.

2. **The `derive` call in githubSource**: `derive(mutexHoldersOf(liveItems, q), liveItems, ...)` — the first arg is the candidate holders derived from live items themselves, and second arg is live items. So phantoms would never be detected? Wait: cand = holders from live items (already filtered to those with the mutex label). liveItems labels: same source. So candSet == labelSet, no phantoms, armedExtra empty, merged = labelHolders. So `liveHolderSet.holders` = labelHolders = mutexHoldersOf(liveItems, q) effectively. That's fine as "the live truth".

The cached set: `derive(holders, items, ...)` where holders is the cached holder list and items is the cached open-PR list from ioCache. If the holder vanished from the cached items list (or labels), it becomes a phantom and is dropped from cachedSet.holders. Hmm — but that's applying the same label-truth filter to the cached snapshot. This means reconciliation compares "cached holders filtered by cached label view" vs "live holders filtered by live label view". Divergence detection: if cached label view shows holder 5 labeled and live shows none → cachedSet.holders=[5], liveHolderSet.holders=[] → divergent → self-heal. OK that works.

But subtle issue: the `reconcile` function checks divergence in both directions; if cached and live agree, no alarm. Fine.

3. **`reconcile` reset counters on non-divergent**: On a non-divergent tick it returns counters of 0 and consecutivePhantomTicks: 0. In githubSource, `recordMutexTickEvent` only called when selfHealed, so non-divergent doesn't record. OK.

But note: `consecutivePhantomTicks` — recordMutexTickEvent merges with mutexTickEvents which is per-tick; the "consecutive" counter in mergeSnapshot: `num(p.consecutivePhantomTicks) + num(e.consecutivePhantomTicks)` — merging snapshot accumulates consecutive ticks but never RESETS when a tick has no phantom events. The published state merges over previous snapshot: `spState.mutex = mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — if spMutex is null (no events this tick) and spPrev.mutex exists, mergeSnapshot(prev, {}) → out.consecutivePhantomTicks = prev.consecutive + 0 = prev — so the "consecutive" counter never resets on a clean tick. A clean tick keeps the previous count and it grows forever. The name `consecutivePhantomTicks` implies reset when no phantom occurs this tick. This is a real bug: consecutive counter semantics broken — it accumulates monotonically (capped? no cap on counters, only alarms capped at 5). So consecutivePhantomTicks grows unboundedly and never resets. Is it consumed anywhere? Let me grep. The I2 invariant says "Silent full-defer of ALL candidates for ≥2 consecutive ticks ... is itself an alarm condition". Also Q2: auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks. Does any code read consecutivePhantomTicks to trigger that? Let me check the code.

Also there's `takeMutexTickSnapshot` resetting mutexTickEvents per tick. But the consecutive counter doesn't reset across ticks in the published state. The per-tick events only get recorded on self-heal. On a tick with no heal, spMutex is null and spState.mutex = mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, null) = keeps prev counters including consecutivePhantomTicks. # Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:

  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}

          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +817
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T21:34:26Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).
