## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

Today's configs only define `mutex: "ai_validating"` (verified in `sm_github.json`), so this is latent — but the moment a second mutex label exists (the `mutexAmong`/parallel-window machinery clearly anticipates more), every full-slot defer for that rule mis-derives: legitimate holders of the other label are not in the `ai_validating` label layer, so the probe classifies them as phantoms, drops the open-PR cache, clears their slots and lets a queued candidate arm — silently breaking serialization in the *other* direction.

// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +1995
- **Deletions**: -185
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:52:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

```

So `rederiveHoldersLive` compares *cached holders of `q.mutex`* against *label holders of `ai_validating`*. Today's configs only define `mutex: "ai_validating"` (verified in `sm_github.json`), so this is latent — but the moment a second mutex label exists (the `mutexAmong`/parallel-window machinery clearly anticipates more), every full-slot defer for that rule mis-derives: legitimate holders of the other label are not in the `ai_validating` label layer, so the probe classifies them as phantoms, drops the open-PR cache, clears their slots and lets a queued candidate arm — silently breaking serialization in the *other* direction.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017

- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:52:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

So `rederiveHoldersLive` compares *cached holders of `q.mutex`* against *label holders of `ai_validating`*. Today's configs only define `mutex: "ai_validating"` (verified in `sm_github.json`), so this is latent — but the moment a second mutex label exists (the `mutexAmong`/parallel-window machinery clearly anticipates more), every full-slot defer for that rule mis-derives: legitimate holders of the other label are not in the `ai_validating` label layer, so the probe classifies them as phantoms, drops the open-PR cache, clears their slots and lets a queued candidate arm — silently breaking serialization in the *other* direction.

// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). ## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017

- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:52:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

So `rederiveHoldersLive` compares *cached holders of `q.mutex`* against *label holders of `ai_validating`*. Today's configs only define `mutex: "ai_validating"` (verified in `sm_github.json`), so this is latent — but the moment a second mutex label exists (the `mutexAmong`/parallel-window machinery clearly anticipates more), every full-slot defer for that rule mis-derives: legitimate holders of the other label are not in the `ai_validating` label layer, so the probe classifies them as phantoms, drops the open-PR cache, clears their slots and lets a queued candidate arm — silently breaking serialization in the *other* direction.

// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). ## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +1995
- **Deletions**: -185
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:52:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

```

So `rederiveHoldersLive` compares *cached holders of `q.mutex`* against *label holders of `ai_validating`*. Today's configs only define `mutex: "ai_validating"` (verified in `sm_github.json`), so this is latent — but the moment a second mutex label exists (the `mutexAmong`/parallel-window machinery clearly anticipates more), every full-slot defer for that rule mis-derives: legitimate holders of the other label are not in the `ai_validating` label layer, so the probe classifies them as phantoms, drops the open-PR cache, clears their slots and lets a queued candidate arm — silently breaking serialization in the *other* direction.

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +1995
- **Deletions**: -185
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:52:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `labelHoldersOf` hardcodes `'ai_validating'` inside a reconciliation path that is generic over `q.mutex`**

The scan/defer machinery in `githubSource` is parameterized by the rule's mutex label (`q.mutex` — see `mutexHoldersOf` at `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:685` and the defer log), but the label-layer leg of the derivation always reads the literal string:

```js
if (labels.indexOf('ai_validating') !== -1) {
```

So `rederiveHoldersLive` compares *cached holders of `q.mutex`* against *label holders of `ai_validating`*. Today's configs only define `mutex: "ai_validating"` (verified in `sm_github.json`), so this is latent — but the moment a second mutex label exists (the `mutexAmong`/parallel-window machinery clearly anticipates more), every full-slot defer for that rule mis-derives: legitimate holders of the other label are not in the `ai_validating` label layer, so the probe classifies them as phantoms, drops the open-PR cache, clears their slots and lets a queued candidate arm — silently breaking serialization in the *other* direction.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.

Nothing drives a full-slot defer scenario through `queryPrs`'s new phantom-heal branch, and nothing drives `rerun_cancelled_checks`'s new ghost-cancel branch in `smAgent`.

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +1995
- **Deletions**: -185
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:52:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `labelHoldersOf` hardcodes `'ai_validating'` inside a reconciliation path that is generic over `q.mutex`**

The scan/defer machinery in `githubSource` is parameterized by the rule's mutex label (`q.mutex` — see `mutexHoldersOf` at `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:685` and the defer log), but the label-layer leg of the derivation always reads the literal string:

```js
if (labels.indexOf('ai_validating') !== -1) {
```

So `rederiveHoldersLive` compares *cached holders of `q.mutex`* against *label holders of `ai_validating`*. Today's configs only define `mutex: "ai_validating"` (verified in `sm_github.json`), so this is latent — but the moment a second mutex label exists (the `mutexAmong`/parallel-window machinery clearly anticipates more), every full-slot defer for that rule mis-derives: legitimate holders of the other label are not in the `ai_validating` label layer, so the probe classifies them as phantoms, drops the open-PR cache, clears their slots and lets a queued candidate arm — silently breaking serialization in the *other* direction.

Thread the label through: `derive(holders, liveItems, isRunConcluded, repo, nowIso, mutexLabel)` with `labelHoldersOf(liveItems, mutexLabel)`, and have `githubSource` pass `q.mutex`. The alarm `detail` string has the same hardcoding and should carry the actual label too.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: required `crap` quality gate is red on the head commit**

CI check `crap` failed on `1c8008e5`. The crap4js ratchet (threshold 8, baseline `crap-baseline`) reports:

```text
REGRESSION  js/factoryState.js::buildFactoryState: 65.1 -> 66.1
REGRESSION  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 67.4 -> 131.8
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateFailureCount: 110
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::normalizeHolder: 36.8
NEW > 8  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::mutexHoldersOf: 56
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::isGhostCancelProbe: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::normalizeMutexSnapshot: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::num: 20
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::derive: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::reconcile: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::mergeSnapshot: 11
2 regression(s), 10 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

The ratchet only ever goes down, so this cannot be fixed by updating the baseline — the new code must be decomposed. Concretely:

- Extract the phantom-heal block added to `queryPrs` into its own function (that block is also what drove the 67.4 → 131.8 regression, and per comment on the `githubApi` guard it is currently unreachable dead weight).
- Split `silentUpdateFailureCount` (110 — the regex-while loop plus counting makes it the worst offender), `mutexHoldersOf` (56), `normalizeHolder` (36.8), `isGhostCancelProbe` (20), `normalizeMutexSnapshot` (20, including its inner `num`).
- `silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12` is a one-liner whose score is coverage-driven — it needs a direct unit test.

The PR description's "Full suite … 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions" is true only for the unit suite; the required CRAP gate is a separate, red merge blocker.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.

### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +1995
- **Deletions**: -185
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:52:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `labelHoldersOf` hardcodes `'ai_validating'` inside a reconciliation path that is generic over `q.mutex`**

The scan/defer machinery in `githubSource` is parameterized by the rule's mutex label (`q.mutex` — see `mutexHoldersOf` at `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:685` and the defer log), but the label-layer leg of the derivation always reads the literal string:

```js
if (labels.indexOf('ai_validating') !== -1) {
```

So `rederiveHoldersLive` compares *cached holders of `q.mutex`* against *label holders of `ai_validating`*. Today's configs only define `mutex: "ai_validating"` (verified in `sm_github.json`), so this is latent — but the moment a second mutex label exists (the `mutexAmong`/parallel-window machinery clearly anticipates more), every full-slot defer for that rule mis-derives: legitimate holders of the other label are not in the `ai_validating` label layer, so the probe classifies them as phantoms, drops the open-PR cache, clears their slots and lets a queued candidate arm — silently breaking serialization in the *other* direction.

Thread the label through: `derive(holders, liveItems, isRunConcluded, repo, nowIso, mutexLabel)` with `labelHoldersOf(liveItems, mutexLabel)`, and have `githubSource` pass `q.mutex`. The alarm `detail` string has the same hardcoding and should carry the actual label too.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

🚨 **BLOCKING: required `crap` quality gate is red on the head commit**

CI check `crap` failed on `1c8008e5`. The crap4js ratchet (threshold 8, baseline `crap-baseline`) reports:

```text

2 regression(s), 10 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed

The ratchet only ever goes down, so this cannot be fixed by updating the baseline — the new code must be decomposed. Concretely:

- Extract the phantom-heal block added to `queryPrs` into its own function (that block is also what drove the 67.4 → 131.8 regression, and per comment on the `githubApi` guard it is currently unreachable dead weight).
- Split `silentUpdateFailureCount` (110 — the regex-while loop plus counting makes it the worst offender), `mutexHoldersOf` (56), `normalizeHolder` (36.8), `isGhostCancelProbe` (20), `normalizeMutexSnapshot` (20, including its inner `num`).
- `silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12` is a one-liner whose score is coverage-driven — it needs a direct unit test.

The PR description's "Full suite … 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions" is true only for the unit suite; the required CRAP gate is a separate, red merge blocker.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no test exercises the new wiring — AC2/AC3 integration paths are untested**

Every hunk in this file (and in `test_smAgent.js` / `test_mergeCadence.js`) only adds `'../../common/mutexRegistry.js': loadModule(...)` to the require maps. Nothing drives a full-slot defer scenario through `queryPrs`'s new phantom-heal branch, and nothing drives `rerun_cancelled_checks`'s new ghost-cancel branch in `smAgent`.

This gap is exactly why the BLOCKING `provider.githubApi` defect slipped through: a single test loading `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module (or a stub shaped like its facade) and asserting the live re-read fires on a full-slot defer would have caught that the guard is unsatisfiable in production.

The ticket's test plan explicitly requires these hooks: IT-1 (scripted two-tick phantom self-heal → AC2), IT-2 (cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe → AC3), plus the REG-1 replay rule ("red REG blocks merge of this fix"). This PR ships only pure-function UTs of `mutexRegistry`; the scripted two-tick scenario and the REG fixture are absent. Please add at least the IT-1/IT-2 level tests against the real provider facade shape before merge.

The once-per-head marker makes the ghost re-dispatch strictly one-shot per head: if the fresh CI run the machine dispatches here gets cancelled again (the gh-748 kicker race is not guaranteed to be gone — the incident that spawned this card was a cancel storm), the next tick finds `ghostProbe.isGhostCancel && ghostGateHeld` true, sees the marker, and takes this branch:

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 15
- **Additions**: +1995
- **Deletions**: -185
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T09:52:09Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `labelHoldersOf` hardcodes `'ai_validating'` inside a reconciliation path that is generic over `q.mutex`**

The scan/defer machinery in `githubSource` is parameterized by the rule's mutex label (`q.mutex` — see `mutexHoldersOf` at `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:685` and the defer log), but the label-layer leg of the derivation always reads the literal string:

```js
if (labels.indexOf('ai_validating') !== -1) {
```

So `rederiveHoldersLive` compares *cached holders of `q.mutex`* against *label holders of `ai_validating`*. Today's configs only define `mutex: "ai_validating"` (verified in `sm_github.json`), so this is latent — but the moment a second mutex label exists (the `mutexAmong`/parallel-window machinery clearly anticipates more), every full-slot defer for that rule mis-derives: legitimate holders of the other label are not in the `ai_validating` label layer, so the probe classifies them as phantoms, drops the open-PR cache, clears their slots and lets a queued candidate arm — silently breaking serialization in the *other* direction.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js

```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-17):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
